result_semantic_payload.summary: The hypothesis that employee 'lihua' exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is NOT supported by the recorded evidence. The only customer database export in the record occurred on 2024-05-10 at 01:03:22 and was performed by the non-interactive service account 'svc_export' as part of the scheduled job 'nightly_export' (triggered 2024-05-09 23:55:01), writing 184,112 customer rows to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz with status=success in 18s. The scheduler definition (/scheduler/jobs.conf) independently corroborates that nightly_export is scheduled daily at 23:55 and runs as svc_export, and /README.txt states svc_export is a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs. The only lihua activity in the log is two FAILED login attempts at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from 198.51.100.44 (reason=password), i.e., roughly 44 minutes AFTER the export completed, with no successful authentication and no EXPORT record under lihua. The evidence therefore attributes the export to the automated scheduler/service account, not to lihua. Note: the delegated source scope was 'windows', but the task exposes no Windows platform scenario and no Windows artifacts (no event log, registry, prefetch/amcache, or file-system timeline) were available; the finding is based on the application log, scheduler config, and README present in the image.

claim_candidates.text: The customer database export on 2024-05-10 was performed by the service account svc_export, not by employee lihua.
The export was an automated scheduled run: job nightly_export was triggered at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 and the export ran 2024-05-10 01:03:22-01:03:40 (18s, success) under account svc_export.
The export produced dataset=customers with 184112 rows written to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz.

lihua had no successful authentication and no EXPORT activity in the record; the only lihua entries are two FAILED logins at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from IP 198.51.100.44 (reason=password), occurring after the export had already completed.

The analyst's hypothesis attributing the export to lihua is unsupported and should be rejected in favor of the scheduled-job explanation; lihua's failed logins from an external-looking IP 30+ minutes after the export are a separate signal worth follow-up.
limitations: No independent authentication log, session, or file-system access record corroborates who touched /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz; attribution rests on application-log account fields plus the scheduler definition.
No evidence shows whether lihua's failed logins relate to the export or to another motive; the ordering alone does not establish intent or knowledge.

claim_candidates.text: svc_export is documented as a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs, consistent with the automated attribution.

limitations: No Windows-derived evidence (event logs, registry, prefetch/amcache, file-system access timeline) was available; execution and authentication claims could not be corroborated with the Windows artifacts the profile normally requires.

The application log is a 440-byte preview; completeness of the log around 2024-05-10 (and any truncation/rotation) is unverified.
File mtime/ctime values are all 1790594134 (2026), so file metadata cannot be used to date or order events.
No evidence addresses whether the exported artifact was later accessed or exfiltrated, and no evidence establishes lihua's intent regarding the failed logins.
